text:
IncidentBot: [ALERT] spike detected: kv_cache_size_growth > 3x baseline on prod-cluster-a (alerts.grafana/redwood)
IncidentBot: top symptoms: token cadence stalls on streaming, elevated tail latency for gpt-redwood-2-small, partial flush errors observed in runtime logs

Tom O'Connor: seeing the alert, paging oncall. I'm oncall right now, pulling traces.

Priya Nair: oncall-sre here, joining. any suspect deploys in the last 30m?

deploy-bot: deploy finished: runtime-service@release/2026-03-15-18:03 (sha: a1b2c3d) to prod-cluster-a (canary 10%)

Alex Chen: that canary pushed the new continuous-batching heuristics and the kv-cache autogrow change. I warned it might change eviction cadence.

Jordan Lee: support reporting 3 customer tickets about streaming stutter and mid-stream stalls — customers: AcmeAnalytics, FluentChat, Notesly. latency spikes and partial responses.

Casey Wu: logs show repeated "kv_cache: growth loop detected" and then "partial_kv_flush: bytes_written=0" on many workers. Looks like eviction isn't freeing entries.

Tom O'Connor: can we throttle or disable continuous batching on the canary asap? That should reduce backlog.

Alex Chen: I can flip a runtime flag for the canary group: set continuous_batching.enabled=false. Doing it now for canary instances.

Alex Chen: DONE for canary. Pushing the same flag to 25% to see effect.

Priya Nair: creating a temporary routing rule to send heavy-streaming customers to fallback model variant (gpt-redwood-2-small-safe) to reduce KV pressure. Jordan, can you prepare comms?

Jordan Lee: yup. Drafting message: "We're investigating intermittent streaming stalls. We've applied mitigations and routed traffic to a safer variant. We'll update in 15m." Will post to affected workspaces when we have confirmation.

Casey Wu: metric update: kv_cache_size growth rate slowed ~35% on canary after disabling continuous batching. However, canary has only 12 hosts — need broader to judge.

Tom O'Connor: escalate to rollback decision if growth resumes when we expand flag. Alex, can you also temporarily cap kv_cache.max_entries to 200k to prevent blowups?

Alex Chen: changing config: 
```
kv_cache.max_entries=200000
kv_cache.eviction_policy=LRU
continuous_batching.window_ms=0  # force immediate flush
```
Applying to prod-cluster-a (first to 50% of hosts).

deploy-bot: runtime-config update applied to 50% of prod-cluster-a hosts.

Priya Nair: watch dashboards for OOM churn, eviction rates, and the streaming token cadence metric. Also set an alert for "partial_kv_flush > 0".

Casey Wu: eviction rate jumped after cap but now stabilizing, partial_kv_flush logs decreasing. No OOMs observed so far.

Elena Park: pinging CS to prep one-off notes for top 3 customers. Jordan, include that there is no data loss and only degraded streaming experience.

Jordan Lee: will do. sending now.

Jordan Lee: (message posted) "We applied temporary routing and config mitigations to reduce streaming stalls. You may see slightly higher latency for some requests. We're monitoring and will follow up in 30 minutes." :white_check_mark:

Tom O'Connor: good. Priya, do you want the oncall handoff in 30m or should I keep it until stable?

Priya Nair: stay oncall until we confirm stability across all hosts, then handoff. I'll take next shift if you need break after resolution.

Alex Chen: expanding config to 100% of prod-cluster-a now. Rolling change with 10s drain between instances.

Casey Wu: after 100% roll, metrics look much better: kv cache growth back to baseline, streaming token cadence recovered to normal for 92% of sessions, partial flush logs near zero.

Tom O'Connor: thanks. Any customer-facing incidents to escalate to incident page?

Jordan Lee: recommended incident message: "Intermittent streaming stalls for some customers due to a runtime regression in continuous batching + kv-cache autogrow. Mitigation: disabled continuous batching heuristics and capped KV cache; routed heavy streaming traffic to safe model variant. Customers may have seen partial responses; no data loss. Full rollback not required. Postmortem to follow."

Priya Nair: agreed. I'll open the incident ticket and assign postmortem to Alex + Casey.

Alex Chen: quick root cause summary: the new heuristic allowed KV entries to keep references from streaming sessions longer than expected; combined with a change in partial flush path that caused no-op flushes, the cache never reclaimed entries and we hit pressure. Continuous batching increased in-flight token windows which amplified the problem.

Casey Wu: reproduction steps noted in runtime tickets. We'll add a unit/regression test for partial_kv_flush edge case and a canary check for kv_cache growth.

Tom O'Connor: handoff: I'm going offline for 30m, Priya will be oncall. Priya, accept handoff?

Priya Nair: accepted. I'll keep monitoring for 60m and then re-evaluate.

Elena Park: CS update sent: customers acknowledged, appreciate quick action. One wants ETA for full fix. Jordan, suggest: "we expect a code-level fix in 48 hours; temporary mitigations are in place."

Jordan Lee: sent.

Tom O'Connor: final checks: set postmortem owner to Alex, label severity=P2, link to ticket and relevant grafana/dashboards.

Priya Nair: creating GitLab issue: "runtime: kv-cache blowup + continuous batching regression" assigned to Alex, reviewers Casey + Priya. Link: https://git.redwood/runtime/issues/4821

Alex Chen: thanks. I'll start the patch: ensure partial_kv_flush returns bytes_written>0 or triggers fallback eviction; add strict max age for KV entries on streaming sessions.

Casey Wu: I'll add monitoring alert changes and a canary gating rule for future continuous-batching toggles.

IncidentBot: Incident updated: status -> mitigated, severity -> P2, owner -> Alex Chen, link -> https://incidents.redwood/1789456123

Tom O'Connor: marking this thread resolved for now. We'll follow up in the postmortem. Great job everyone. :bow:
